article.articleSummary: Delhi's air quality is linked to rising illness, including human H1N1 swine flu cases this year. article.articleSummary: Schistosomiasis transmission in China depends on the snail Oncomelania hupensis. article.articleHeadline: What should everyone do to prevent emerging infectious diseases?
article.articleSummary: Emerging infectious diseases can appear suddenly and threaten health; prevention hinges on public measures and individual actions. Avoid wildlife and sick animals; report unusual animal deaths. Prevent vectors by removing standing water, covering containers, nets, and repellents, especially where dengue and Zika circulate. Seek prompt medical care for high fever, breathing difficulty, severe symptoms, or dehydration, and follow health authorities. A healthy lifestyle supports immunity but cannot replace vaccines or targeted defenses.

article.articleHeadline: Hantavirus infects wildlife farmers in Vietnam: A risk to Southeast Asia
article.articleSummary: Vietnam wildlife farming (6,744 farms, 1.8 million animals across 371 species by 2021) poses hantavirus spillover risk. A 2023–2024 study of 210 farmers in Lao Cai and Dong Nai found nearly 9% IgG positivity and 1.9% active infections; no outbreaks were reported. Antibody tests indicate prior exposure; no viral RNA was detected, and the specific hantavirus variant remains unidentified. Infections may stem from exposure to infected wild rodents outside farms; transmission is via inhalation of dust contaminated with urine, droppings, or saliva. The findings underscore Southeast Asia risk, including Indonesia, and the need for genetic confirmation (RT-PCR/sequencing) and strengthened surveillance. Preventive actions include protective equipment, One Health collaboration, and stricter wildlife farming enforcement. In 2025, Andes hantavirus caused a shipborne outbreak on MV Hondius in South America: 13 infections and 3 deaths, likely started ashore with onward person-to-person spread.

article.articleHeadline: Severe Covid-19 'could reawaken dormant viruses' and make symptoms even worse
article.articleSummary: Severe Covid-19 can reawaken dormant viruses in the body. In a Nature study of 1,154 adults hospitalized with Covid-19, about 550 (nearly half) showed reactivation of at least one latent virus, with 11 reactivations within 40 days of admission. Reactivation correlated with increased inflammation and contributed to long Covid symptoms such as fatigue and reduced ability to walk and dress. Regular blood samples and nasal swabs tracked viral RNA to confirm lingering viruses after acute infection. Globally, the WHO reported about 6,800 Covid-19 cases, while the UK estimates around 2 million people (roughly 3%) have long Covid. Thai researchers noted new coronaviruses circulating in bats, underscoring why understanding immune triggers and developing antivirals is urgent, says Esther Melamed of the University of Texas.

article.articleHeadline: Two domestic Mpox Ib cases reported
article.articleSummary: Taiwan reports two domestically acquired mpox (monkeypox) cases of Clade Ib, both in men in their 30s and unvaccinated; onset in late July and early August. As of Aug 23, Taiwan has 28 confirmed mpox cases this year (19 domestic, 9 imported); total since June 2022 is 544 (500 domestic, 44 imported). Most cases are young to middle-aged men; many have engaged in unsafe sex; about 90% lack mpox vaccination. Vaccination remains the best preventive measure and protects both Clade Ib and Clade II; Tecovirimat is available for severe Ib infections. In Asia, June 8–July 19 saw 29 cases in Thailand, with the remainder in Africa.

article.articleHeadline: An 8-year-old girl who swam in a lake died the day after her birthday... What is the 'brain-eating amoeba' that attacked the brain?
article.articleSummary: An 8-year-old girl from Ruston, Louisiana, died from Naegleria fowleri infection after swimming in Claybon Lake during a family trip. Naegleria fowleri, a free-living amoeba in warm freshwater, can enter the nose and migrate to the brain, causing primary amebic meningoencephalitis (PAM), a rapidly progressive and nearly always fatal brain infection. CDC data show 180 PAM cases in the United States from 1937–2025, typically 0–8 per year, with mortality over 97%. The patient, Lillian Smart, began treatment Aug 15 and died the next day; early symptoms—headache, fever, nausea, vomiting—arise about 5 days after exposure, followed by neck stiffness, confusion, balance problems, seizures, hallucinations, and coma. Prevention focuses on avoiding nasal water entry in warm freshwater: use nose plugs, avoid diving, and use safe water for nasal rinses. Person-to-person transmission does not occur. Korea also reported its first domestic PAM case in 2022: a man who had stayed in Thailand died.

article.articleHeadline: Scientists Warn That a New Coronavirus Affecting Humans May Emerge from Cambodia Soon!
article.articleSummary: Cambodian bats in Steung Treng province yielded four sarbecovirus groups with potential to cross species barriers. From Aug 2020 to Jun 2023, researchers collected samples from 1,462 bats across nine genera; 146 samples tested positive for at least one coronavirus. Genetic analyses produced 33 complete genomes of previously uncharacterized sarbecoviruses. Recombination was frequent, and Cambodian viruses showed evolutionary links to viruses detected in Vietnam and Thailand, indicating regional movement beyond borders. Notably, spike proteins from groups 2 and 3 had receptor-binding domains with up to 96.8% amino-acid identity to SARS-CoV-2, and pseudovirus experiments demonstrated entry into cells via human ACE2 for a representative group-2 spike. However, isolated viruses were not recovered, so there is no evidence of current human infection or human-to-human spread. Notably, viruses lacked the SARS-CoV-2 polybasic furin cleavage site. Surveillance remains important given high diversity and recombination. The findings were published in Nature Communications.

article.articleHeadline: Malaria: What triggers it and how to recognize it.
article.articleSummary: Six Frankfurt Airport employees contracted malaria, with one death, likely from a female Anopheles mosquito that arrived on a flight from an endemic area. Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites; P. falciparum is the most dangerous. In 2022, Africa sub-Saharan regions bore the majority of cases and deaths from malaria, with hundreds of millions of cases and hundreds of thousands of deaths, many children under five. Symptoms typically appear about 7–15 days after a bite and include fever, severe headache, vomiting, diarrhea, sweats and chills. Diagnosis relies on clinical assessment, microscopy, rapid immunochromatographic tests, and sometimes molecular methods. Treatment for P. falciparum malaria uses artemisinin-based combination therapy. Vector control emphasizes insecticide-treated nets, indoor residual spraying, and larval reduction. Two WHO-approved vaccines, RTS,S/AS01 (Mosquirix) and R21/Matrix-M, are reducing child mortality; RTS,S since 2021; R21 deployed in Ghana and Nigeria since 2023, and vaccination expanded to 17 African countries by 2024.
